plan.title: Lung treated vs control DE (batch-confounded, flagged)
plan.analytical_narrative: The counts (12000 genes x 12 samples, from salmon) and metadata show a 6-vs-6 treated/control design in which batch B1 holds every control and batch B2 holds every treated sample — batch is perfectly confounded with condition. No statistical method can separate a condition effect from a batch effect in this design: any batch-correction or batch-adjustment step (ComBat-seq, ~batch+condition, removeBatchEffect, SVA) would either fail (rank-deficient model matrix) or silently remove/inflate the condition signal it purports to preserve. Per the sourced rule (R-0005), the correct path is to fit condition alone, run the standard DESeq2 pipeline, and label every downstream result — DE genes, fold changes, and enriched pathways — as confounded with processing batch, not causally attributable to treatment. The plan runs: (1) sample-structure QC (blinded VST, PCA, distance heatmap) to show explicitly that batch and condition co-vary on the same axis, which is the empirical proof of the confound rather than an assumption; (2) minimal low-count pre-filtering; (3) DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization; (4) DESeq2 Wald test with condition (control as reference) as the sole model term; (5) apeglm shrinkage of the fold changes; (6) BH-adjusted results with independent filtering at alpha 0.05; (7) fgsea preranked enrichment (Wald statistic) against Hallmark, then Reactome and WikiPathways as second-pass collections, using locally staged human GMTs; (8) a report step that states the confound explicitly, gives all required reproducibility fields, and warns the reader that 'treated vs control' and 'batch B2 vs B1' are statistically indistinguishable in this dataset — so any gene called DE could equally be a batch artifact of library prep, sequencing lane, or processing date rather than a treatment effect.
